cards.title: The Prop Drilling Problem
cards.content:
In React, data is typically passed top-down via props. However, when deeply nested components require access to a global piece of state (like a theme, language, or authenticated user), passing props through every intermediate component becomes highly tedious.

This pain point is known as Prop Drilling. It clutters component code and makes maintenance difficult.

// Prop drilling example:
function App() {
  return <Parent theme="dark" />;
}

function Parent({ theme }) {
  return <Child theme={theme} />;
}

function Child({ theme }) {
  return <GrandChild theme={theme} />;
}

cards.title: Creating & Providing Context
cards.content:
React Context provides a way to pass data through the component tree without having to pass props down manually at every level.

It consists of three primary elements:

  • createContext: Initializes a new context instance.
  • Provider: A component wrapper that delivers the context value to all nested components.
  • useContext: A Hook that reads the current value of the context.
import { createContext } from 'react';

// 1. Create the context
export const ThemeContext = createContext('light');

// 2. Provide the value
function App() {
  return (
    <ThemeContext.Provider value="dark">
      <Parent />
    </ThemeContext.Provider>
  );
}

cards.title: Order the Steps of Context Setup

content.description: Arrange the steps to properly implement and consume a Context API solution in React:

items.text: Declare and export the context instance using React.createContext().
Wrap the relevant parent component hierarchy with the context Provider component.
Pass the dynamic data payload to the Provider's 'value' prop.
Import the context and useContext hook in child components to access the value.

cards.title: Context Performance & Best Practices
cards.content:
While Context is incredibly powerful, it has a notable drawback: performance. Every time the context value changes, all consumer components of that context will re-render automatically, regardless of which properties they actually use.

Tips to optimize:

  • Split Contexts: Create distinct, dedicated contexts for values that change at different rates (e.g., separate UserAuthContext from ThemeContext).
  • Memoize Values: Wrap the context value in a useMemo hook to prevent unnecessary object reference changes during parent re-renders.
  • Use State Managers for Fast State: Avoid using Context for high-frequency state updates (e.g., mouse coordinates or complex input forms).
